prompt: An arithmetic sequence starts at $a_1 = 5$ and adds $d = 4$ each step. Find $a_{10}$.
hint: Use $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$. The first term has taken ZERO jumps, not one.

hints.text: Use $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$. The first term has taken ZERO jumps, not one.
To reach term $10$ you take $10 - 1 = 9$ jumps of size $4$, which is $36$ in all. Add that to the first term.
Adding the jumps to the start gives $a_{10} = 5 + 36 = 41$.

explanation: The formula for an arithmetic sequence is $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$, because term $n$ is $n - 1$ jumps past the first.
Substituting the given numbers for the tenth term gives $a_{10} = 5 + (10 - 1) \times 4$.
Multiplying before adding, this is the same as $5 + 9 \times 4 = 5 + 36$.
So the tenth term of the sequence is $a_{10} = 41$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the jumps
steps: Term $1$ is $5$ with no jumps, term $2$ is $9$ after one jump, and term $3$ is $13$ after two jumps.
The number of jumps is always one less than the term number, so term $10$ takes $9$ jumps.
Nine jumps of $4$ add $36$, so the tenth term is $5 + 36 = 41$.

alternativeExplanations.title: List it out
steps: Write the terms by adding $4$ each time: $5, 9, 13, 17, 21, 25, 29, 33, 37, 41$.
Count the entries to be sure the list stops at the right place, and there are exactly ten.
The tenth entry in the list is $41$, so $a_{10} = 41$.
